title: Microsoft 365 admin center: Microsoft Copilot usage report for GCC High and DoD
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, reporting permissions, licensing statement and privacy control are supported by Microsoft sources. The report-opening path needs only a small correction to include a heading omitted from the documented route.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The roadmap introduces a Microsoft 365 Copilot usage report in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 admin center – New Microsoft 365 Copilot usage report for GCC High & DoD

claims.claim: The roadmap says the report will cover total enabled users.
claims.quote: This report will include total enabled and active users

claims.claim: The roadmap says the report will cover total active users.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether the report appears for administrators automatically or requires an enablement setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Copilot usage report GCC High DoD automatically available default enable administrator setting. Read roadmap, usage report, usage reports overview and reporting options; these state availability and viewing steps, not an automatic-arrival or enablement default.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The report is included under the Microsoft Copilot overview's stated Microsoft 365 (Basic) or Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) licence requirement.
claims.quote: In contrast, the Microsoft Copilot usage report focuses on usage of Microsoft Copilot within Microsoft 365 apps such as Teams, Outlook, Word, Excel, and PowerPoint (requires Microsoft 365 (Basic) or Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) licenses).

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The report and reporting-options pages specify viewer roles but do not state whether the viewing administrator personally needs a licence.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Copilot usage report viewing administrator license required reporting viewer prerequisites. Read usage report, reporting options and usage reports overview; licence mentions concern reported users, while viewer requirements name permissions, not a personal licence.

claims.claim: The privacy control is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Org settings > Services > Reports > Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.
claims.quote: Select Org Settings. On the Services tab, select Reports. In the Reports panel, uncheck the checkbox next to Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.

claims.claim: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/reportSettings updates the report privacy setting.
The privacy setting is tenant-wide and applies to all Microsoft 365 usage reports, including Copilot, rather than only this report.
claims.quote: Update tenant-level settings for Microsoft 365 reports. If set to true, all reports conceal user information such as usernames, groups, and sites. If false, all reports show identifiable information.

claims.where: summary; controls[0].note; Why it matters; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Global administrators can change the setting to reveal concealed identifying information.
claims.quote: Global administrators can update the settings to display concealed information if your organization's privacy practices allow it.

claims.claim: The Graph request body uses displayConcealedNames to set whether identifying information is concealed.
claims.quote: displayConcealedNames | Boolean | If set to true, all reports conceal user information such as usernames, groups, and sites. If false, all reports show identifiable information. This property represents a setting in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Required.

claims.claim: The org privacy setting also applies to Microsoft 365 usage reports in Microsoft Graph.
claims.quote: This setting also applies to the Microsoft 365 usage reports in Microsoft Graph and Power BI

claims.claim: The org privacy setting also applies to Microsoft 365 usage reports in Power BI.
claims.quote: This setting also applies to the Microsoft 365 usage reports in Microsoft Graph and Power BI

claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version in Microsoft Graph are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Enabled Users counts unique users with Microsoft Copilot licences during the selected timeframe.
claims.quote: Enabled Users shows the total number of unique users in your organization with Microsoft Copilot licenses over the selected timeframe.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Active Users counts enabled users who tried a user-initiated Copilot feature in one or more Microsoft 365 apps during the selected timeframe.
claims.quote: Active Users shows the total number of enabled users in your organization who tried a user-initiated Microsoft Copilot feature, in one or more apps in Microsoft 365 over the selected timeframe.

claims.claim: The report has an adoption-by-app chart showing enabled and active Copilot users in Microsoft 365 apps.
claims.quote: In the Adoption section, Adoption by app shows enabled users and active users of Copilot in Microsoft 365 apps.

claims.claim: The report includes prompts-submitted metrics.
claims.quote: Total prompts submitted shows the total number of prompts users sent to Microsoft Copilot Chat during the selected time frame.

claims.claim: The report includes Copilot Chat adoption information.
claims.quote: Copilot Chat adoption shows enabled users and total usage of Copilot Chat and split usage between Copilot Chat (work) and Copilot Chat (web).

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment
claims.claim: The report contains a user-level last-activity table.
claims.quote: You can view a table list to show each Microsoft Copilot enabled user's last activity date among Microsoft Copilot apps.

claims.claim: The report offers timeframes of 7, 28, 90 or 180 days.
claims.quote: You can view the Microsoft Copilot report over the last 7, 28, 90, or 180 days.

claims.claim: Activity for a given day typically becomes available within 48 hours of the end of that day in UTC.
claims.quote: For Copilot activity on a given day, the report typically becomes available within 48 hours of the end of that day (in UTC).

claims.claim: The general usage report page does not describe a separate GCC High or DoD variant or its differing metrics, columns or timeframes.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Copilot usage report GCC High DoD metrics columns timeframes organizational messages differences. Read the full usage report and usage reports overview; the latter states cloud availability, but neither describes separate government-cloud report metrics.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Usernames, display names, groups and sites are hidden in usage reports by default.
claims.quote: By default, user-specific information like usernames, display names, groups, and sites is hidden in usage reports.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure and Security & identity
claims.claim: Showing names makes individual usage identifiable to report readers with user-details access, subject to the two no-user-details roles described later.
claims.quote: Global administrators can update the settings to display concealed information if your organization's privacy practices allow it. Usage Summary Reports Reader (with no user details). User Experience Success Manager (with no user details)

claims.claim: The user-level table includes users licensed at any point in the past 180 days, including former licence holders.
claims.quote: The user-level table in the report shows all users who were licensed for Microsoft Copilot at any point over the past 180 days, even if the user later removed the license or never had any Copilot active usage.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Showing identifiable user information is logged in the Microsoft Purview portal audit log.
claims.quote: Showing identifiable user information is a logged event in the Microsoft Purview portal audit log.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes activity reporting and does not state whether organizational messaging is available in this government-cloud report.
claims.quote: This report will include total enabled and active users, Copilot usage with a breakout per Microsoft 365 app, and user-level activity insights (anonymized by default). #copilotcontrolsystem

claims.claim: Aggregates built from audit logs might differ from corresponding official usage-report metrics.
claims.quote: Any aggregated metrics that you build on top of this data, such as "prompt count" or "active user count," might not be consistent with the corresponding data points in the official Copilot usage reports provided by Microsoft.

claims.claim: Client events for Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OneNote and Outlook Copilot can upload late.
claims.quote: For various reasons, uploading client events data for Copilot features in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OneNote, and Outlook can be delayed.

claims.claim: No meter or charge for reading the report is documented at the time of writing in November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Copilot usage report reporting cost price billing meter charge. Read usage report, reporting options and Copilot overview; search excerpts on Copilot billing and Credits describe metered Copilot services, not a meter or charge for reading this report.

claims.claim: The Recommendations card links to the Microsoft Copilot Dashboard in Viva Insights, a separate reporting product.
claims.quote: In Recommendations, the recommended action card highlights Microsoft Copilot Dashboard, where you can deliver insights to your IT leaders to explore Copilot readiness, adoption, and impact in Viva Insights.

claims.claim: The roadmap does not specify which users can view the report.
claims.quote: We will be introducing a new Usage report covering Microsoft 365 Copilot. This report will include total enabled and active users, Copilot usage with a breakout per Microsoft 365 app, and user-level activity insights (anonymized by default). #copilotcontrolsystem

claims.claim: The report opens through Microsoft 365 admin center > Reports > Usage > Microsoft Copilot > Copilot, then the Usage tab.
claims.quote: On the Usage page, under Reports, select Microsoft Copilot, and then select Copilot. On the report page, select the Usage tab to view adoption and usage metrics.
claims.fix: Include the non-selectable Reports heading on the Usage page: 'Microsoft 365 admin center > Reports > Usage > Reports > Microsoft Copilot > Copilot > Usage', as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/admin/activity-reports/microsoft-365-copilot-usage.

claims.claim: Chart data can be exported as CSV.
claims.quote: You can export the report data into an Excel .csv file by selecting the ellipses and then Export in the top corner of the chart.

claims.where: Scope; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The user-level table can be exported as CSV.
claims.quote: To export the report data into an Excel .csv file, select Export. This action exports the usage data of all users and enables you to do simple sorting, filtering, and searching for further analysis.
